He was learning the clarinet about the same time as I was learning the trumpet. I mean the cornet. His name was Elliot Taylor.…

251.s: Bagby was nicknamed Funny because he was comical; the young musicians teased him and he blew his stack.
251.q: F-U-N-N-Y, because he was a funny man. What did he do? Just comical and funny. Little bit of fella, little small guy. Did some funny things.

So you would ask the guy about that and you would tell you, well that's the end for the people in town.…

70.t: How he got the name Butter in McKinney's band
70.s: Don Redman nicknamed him Butter because he looked tender and plump when he joined McKinney's Cotton Pickers on December 7, 1930.
70.q: And they looked at me and, I don't know, they looked at me and I don't know whether my complexion had anything to do with it or not, but Don said I looked like butter.

He -- But he wasn't a guy that you could kid with or nothing, either. Of course, sometimes Tyree used to get to him.

634.t: How he got the name Happy
634.s: A boyhood friend, a piano player named Tom, started calling him Happy because he was jolly and acted in concerts; he also played with Tom Benton.
634.q: Well, when I was a boy, a little kid, I used to always could, I always was a jolly. I used to play in concerts and different things, and I was acting. And so a boy, what he used to be, was he was the one who started to call me happy. And ever since that people called me happy all over the world.

634.t: How Happy got his nickname; other Happys
634.s: A girl first called him Happy; he became Black Happy, with Red Hat; Remus Matthew was another Happy.

765.t: Nicknames of musicians: Newfoot, Fonz the goat boy, Putty

765.t: How Fazola got his nickname from Louis Prima
765.s: Prima's coinage of 'Fazola' from the Italian for beans, and Fazola's reply nickname for Prima.

194.t: How he got the name Professor Longhair

881.t: How he got the nickname Nosey
881.s: His nickname came from his habit of wanting to learn by listening to better players.

400.q: [Laugh] My first one was Sporty. I guess my mother dressed me in Little Lord Fauntaroy suits and things. Then they called me… I started playing violin, they called me Black [Unintelligible] in school because I‟m playing violin. I had a tough time. I wore glasses, 13 years old with a violin and then…

400.s: Ben Webster's slang vocabulary and Cab's Hipsters Dictionary lead Taylor and Hinton to talk about coded talk among musicians.
400.ch: Cab Calloway's band: road, arrangers and shows
400.q: Oh, yeah. And they had that lingo. I‟ll never forget the language those guys used to use. Like Ben Webster was a master at this, the languages. His vocabulary… automobile was a short, and let‟s see, $100 was cow and $50 was a calf. He‟d say, “You see that dude going on out with”… he‟s got that”… he…

80.s: Autrey tells how seeing Sedric eat pie in a camel-hair coat outside a diner made the band call him Honey Bear.
80.q: Well -- (Laughs) -- that's a good story. We were on our way out somewhere, New York state, and we stopped at a diner for coffee and whatnot, and when we came out, we were sitting on the bus waiting for him. He had on one of those -- (laughs) -- one of those coats, a camel-hair, remember those brown…

80.t: Fats gets him back; why Fats called him Hymie
80.s: Fats couldn't stand it and made Kirkeby call Hermie back; the nickname Hymie came from a girl in Philadelphia calling for him, and Fats picked it up.
80.ch: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
80.q: Yes, I had to -- he couldn't stand it any longer, and he made Kirkaby, and everybody else, call me to get Herman back, you know. And I was glad and he was glad, and we were happy. We united, and -- Oh Hymie! Hymie, it's so good to see you! Like that.

88.t: Lee Young's name Leonidas and how his father chose it
88.s: Willard asks about his full name; he explains it was given by his schoolteacher father, who liked Greek history, and that he went by Lee from high school.
88.q: Well, I haven't used that name. The only time that name was ever really used was when I was in Junior High School. All the teachers called me Leonidas Leonidis. But when I got to high school, it was Lee, because, you know, it'd kind of a difficult name, and they pronounced it Leonetis, Leonatis,…

88.t: Ralph Gleason's writing and Lester's private language and nicknames
88.s: Lee thinks only Ralph Gleason captured Lester and discusses Lester's slang and nicknames like Ripty Gipty for Paul Campbell.
88.q: the people that have written things about Lester, that I have read, I only know one that really captured him that made me, you know, as his brother, sitting down reading it, thinking that that person really got to Lester, got to know Lester -- and that was Ralph Gleason.

378.s: Mildred gave names to everyone: Bing the Groaner, Pops Whiteman, and Dance 'Oaks'.
378.ch: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
378.q: But Mildred during those times -- Mildred always had names for everybody --

378.t: Paul Ash and the Oriental Theater: Norville becomes Norvo
378.s: Jack Tebo gets him a single with Paul Ash on the Publix circuit; when Ash garbles his name Variety prints Red Norvo, and he keeps it.
378.q: And I really always wanted to write, all those early years, when I was -- when I later became a single in vaudeville, I made a-- quite a bit of money doing a single. The same Jack Tiboo got me with Paul Ash on the [Publix] Circuit and I was working a single, I was maybe 18-19 years old. 19 I guess.…

167.t: Meeting Eddie Lang through Paul Whiteman
167.s: Bunn met guitarist Eddie Lang in New York years ago, when Lang was with Paul Whiteman.
167.ch: Spirits of Rhythm and the road in the 1930s
167.q: I met Eddy Lang in New York, years ago. With Paul Whiteman.

167.t: Where the name Spirits of Rhythm came from
167.s: The members were from St. Louis; under Ben Bernie they were the Sepia Nephews and then took the Spirits of Rhythm name.
167.q: Yeah, that's right. We just took that name, the Spirits of Rhythm, the Four Spirits of Rhythm, the Six Spirits of Rhythm, and that's as far as we went. Ben Burnie's Sepia Nephews.

381.s: Hinton opens the interview in Nice, France; Francis explains that Roy Eldridge called him Panama at his first rehearsal because of his Panama hat.
381.q: It's David Albert Francis. I didn't get the name Panama until I came to New York in 1938, and I joined Roy Eldridge's band. I came to rehearsal for the first time with a Panama hat on; I'd just come from Florida, and that was what they were wearing down there at that time during the summer.

381.t: Joining Roy's band and being christened Panama
381.s: His first week with Roy, the hat prompted the name Panama, which stuck; only people who knew him before 1939 call him David.
381.ch: Billy Hicks, the Apollo and Roy Eldridge
381.q: July, and that's when my name was changed from David to Panama. That's the reason when I meet someone that calls me David right now, it's someone that knew me before 1939. You know, you can always tell the people who knew me before 1939, because they would call me David, with the exception of a few…

93.t: Why Joe Steele was called Peckin': heel work and music appreciation
93.s: The interviewers ask whether the nickname came from heel work; Green says Steele called it music appreciation and credits a Conway for the pecking step.
93.ch: Split, hospital and decline of tap
93.q: Yes, he calls that -- what do he call that? He says he's got a title for it -- he says -- music appreciation. That's what he calls it -- music appreciation, see, dropping of the heels (unintelligible) like say, for instance, if you're playing staccato, see, and you go into what you call the…

93.t: Naming steps like Ride the Horse as a private language
93.s: J. D. named steps such as Ride the Horse, scissors and thread the needle; Green demonstrates and they built an act with their own vocabulary.
93.ch: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
93.q: place the steps and so forth, what to name the steps. See, Slim, when he would dance, if he'd do a step, he'd give the step a name, you know, like ride the horse or something like that, you know.

388.t: How Milt Hinton got the nickname 'Judge'
388.s: Leeman asks and Hinton explains that his nickname began when he arrived early at studios and greeted everyone, echoing his grandmother's story of a jailed man and the judge.
388.q: And I think that since you are my interviewer on these tapes, that you should tell the people how come you were named the judge.

388.s: Hinton asks about names; Leeman reveals his unused middle name Spencer, after a grandfather.
388.q: Well, I never liked it so I never used it. I was named for Clifford Spencer -- was after my grandfather.

149.t: Dropping the Collegians name for Erskine Hawkins and his band
149.s: The school started another Collegians, so the band became Erskine Hawkins and his band in 1934-35.
149.ch: Forming the band in New York
149.q: Oh, well, the school originated another 'Bama State Collegians. So, we had to give that name up on account it's a school name.

149.t: How he got the name Erskine Ramsey Hawkins
149.s: His birth certificate said Johnny Hawkins and he changed it.
149.ch: Band family, war years and wrap-up
149.q: And, you don't know how I got my name. My mother was working at this school in Birmingham called Erskine Ramsey High. And, my mother and the president, you know, the president liked my mother very much. She was back there in the kitchen, making, cooking, you know, things like that.

413.t: Ben Webster's hip language and Cab's dictionary
413.s: Webster collected slang, and Cab picked it up for his dictionary.
413.ch: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
413.q: Oh, yeah. I memorized some of them. He would pick these things up, he said he overheard this couple in the next room, a guy seducing a girl, and he loved these lines.

413.t: Strutting With Some Barbecue and Beaucoup Jack
413.s: Maxwell explains West Coast and Creole slang in Armstrong titles.
413.ch: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
413.q: Well, that's something that always interested me. You know, many black people don't know the meaning of that song, "Strutting With Some Barbeque," but that was a West Coast expression for a good looking girl, barbeque. I remember it, it was popular when I lived there. I guess Louis must have…

78.t: How Fletcher got the nickname Smack, and Horace 'Little Smack'
78.s: Horace doesn't know the origin of 'Smack'; he heard it came from Fletcher being a kisser. He was called Little Smack to distinguish them.
78.ch: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
78.q: Huh! I don't know. They call me Little Smack, and I just -- I think I was given that name just with the Little put on it, just the distinction between the two of us. But I have heard that he was quite a kisser.

78.s: The interviewer recalls picking up bebop talk at sixteen; Horace says musicians had their own slang, like a hipsters' dictionary, such as 'axe' for horn.
78.ch: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
78.q: Oh, absolutely. As we say, that's slang. You know? In fact, Tom, somewhere around the house here I've got a book, just a small book, that it was put out by a guy that would have the musical slang in there, and he would have that expression, and then on the opposite side of the word he would…

172.s: His nickname Bebe came from his sister and he drew crowds under it.
172.q: Big Baby? Big Baby. That's, and I'm telling you brothers, they're famous too. That's what, no hollerin' about, no my name was William. They'd be a rich little. That's all they called them. Everybody, even their white people, you see, go. They got their called in there. Now when I started, around up…

864.t: Why he is called Bird: a Filipino sailor in the Navy
864.s: A Filipino sailor in the Navy could not say Wilbert and called him Bird; his high chest fit.
864.q: That's, uh, he could never say Wilbert, so he just said, well, I'll call you Bird. And he started to call me Bird, and from then on everybody started calling me Bird. Mm-hmm. That was a Filipino boy, originally, was young. Mm-hmm.

244.s: Talk about New Orleans nicknames, including Fleming's own, Louis Nelson's and Earl Bostic's.
244.q: I had Cuz because I used to call everybody Cousin. Yeah. And if I didn't know your name, I'd say, hi Cuz. So, that was pleasant to see everybody accepted as such.

248.t: Why they called him Rat: passing the hat
248.s: Dawson explains his nickname Rat, given by Alphonse Picou, because he was the one willing to pass the hat and could drop coins into his palm.
248.ch: Fish fries, passing the hat and district living
248.q: Well, uh, you see, I used to be sneaking around, you know. Steaking around with the women or the money? No, the money. Because it set me to collect money, I'd go, I'd make the rock going back in Tar-kun, take half of the money out there.

815.t: Why he went to Europe and how he got the name Satchmo
815.s: Armstrong says he wanted to go blow for them, first stopping in London. A British editor greeted him at Plymouth with 'Satchmo', which stuck.
815.q: place i just want to get over there and blow them cuts the first place i went was london they ain't never put that in the book yet i mean nat canelo the trumpet man of england in those days and he's the one that had to have my suit pressed so i could make this musical musician conference i mean…

250.t: From Red Hot band to High Society Six to Stu Bergen's New Orleans style
250.s: He explains choosing the Red Hot name, dropping it after the Druids raid, then High Society Six and finally his own name for hotel work.
250.q: When I was a little kid I always did like Devil Ham. You know anything? Trademark is the Devil. And I said what can I do for a name that will be before the public in other subjects, other phases? Like a Red Hot sale going on. So I must have seen that one day. So I said Berg if you go ahead and take…

861.t: Biloxi, Bob Burns and the name 'bazooka'
861.s: The group was taken to a Biloxi hotel where Bob Burns saw Johnson's horn and later named it the bazooka; they discuss how it is blown.
861.q: He said, oh you didn't hear no talk of him. He wasn't known then. Wasn't thanks. Or nothing like that until 29. After he saw my horn. And in 1929, in 28, then you begin to hear talk of Bob Burns and Ben Crosby. And he named the horn the bazooka. So after everybody saw me play that, they started…

955.t: How Albert Walters got the name Fernandez and the nickname Badda
955.s: He explains that his stepfather's name stuck as Fernandez, and that Paul Barbarin nicknamed him Badda, advertising him as Kid Badda.
955.q: Well, my stepfather raised me and that name just followed Fernandez. And practically all the older musicians know me by the name of Fernandez. I mean my son, Albert's son is a trumpet player and he introduced himself and nobody knows, he's older people, so you've got to explain the name of…

474.s: Jones's group was called the Rinky Dinks, a name taken from the funny papers.
474.ch: New Orleans bands: Cheek, Parker, Morgan
474.q: What are the Rinky Dinks? That was my group. I had a group by that name and they had some other group downtown too. But I had a group by that name.

259.t: How the Liberty Bell band got its name
259.s: Vincent says he chose the name from novels he read about the Liberty Boys of '76. The band became popular and its alumni became known worldwide.
259.ch: Banjo career, Armstrong and the Liberty Bell
259.q: You know, I used to read them novels all the time. You know, the British and the, the soldiers and the fight. You know, like the comedy book. I had to read that all the time. And it says, the Liberty Boys are 76. And I just picked out the Liberty Bell, you know.

623.s: He explains he was named Richard Charles Howard Smith to distinguish him among relatives.
623.q: Well, I was born into the Smith clan. My name is Richard, and to make me different, they decided to name me Richard Charles Howard Smith. A lot of relatives got in the act there.

184.t: Tubby's age and how Fred Hall became Tubby
184.s: Tubby was two years older, born around 1895; his real name was Fred Hall and he was nicknamed for being fat, with Minor called Little Tubby.
184.q: Well, let me see. He was, I was two years older than him, and I was born in 97, so I met him. He was born, I don't know what month, but that's your name, born in 95. 95.

956.t: How he got the nickname Chicken and what the J stands for
956.s: Henry explains that WPA co-workers called him Chicken Man, shortened to Chick, and that J is Joseph; a visitor interrupts.
956.q: No, I don't mind telling us. You see, when we was out in the field, on the WPA, I knew more about chickens than any other fellow out there. In fact, at one time, I could tell you, name every part of a chicken from the top of his comb down to the bottom of his feet. And from his build to his tail.…

577.t: How he got the nickname Sunshine
577.s: Froeberg called him Sunshine in Memphis and the name stuck in New York; he was listed as Jack Sunshine on a record.
577.q: Oh man that's a long story. Froeberg tacked that name on me. We were playing in Memphis in the Peabody Hotel and we were going up to the roof to play a session, a luncheon session or something and I don't know, he started talking like a colored guy, you know, and he said something about Sunshine,…

922.t: Spelling and pronunciation of the Cottrell name
922.s: The name is spelled Cottrell, once Cottrelle, often mispronounced Contrell or Cantrell.
922.q: C-O-T-R-E-L-L, that's the way we register. Two L's. That's right. And truthfully, the name is really C-O-T-R-E-L-L-E. My father dropped it somewhere and that's the way we all registered. It used to be Cottrell, the way they would pronounce it.

957.t: How he got the nickname Chinee
957.s: Foster explains that playing in white and colored bands as a long-haired boy, people took him for Mexican, Spanish or Indian, and a 'Chinee' act on a show gave him the name.
957.q: You see, when I first started, as I told you once before, I was a little kid. I'll be 61 on the 19th of March, St. Joseph Cummins. Born 1900, I'm with the year. Well, I got the name of Chai Nee by playing with white and colored bands. See, when I was a little boy, well, musicians wasn't like you…

83.t: City directory spellings of the Matassa name
83.s: The interviewer reads directory listings for Vincent Matassa and variant spellings; Matassa explains the name means skein.
83.q: That's because they mispronounced... It misspelled his name. They just misspelled it? Sure. That was my father's uncle, the one that he came to work...

266.t: Calling elders Mr. and why everyone said Jack for Teagarden
266.s: Jones explains the habit of calling older people Mr., never calling Jack Teagarden anything else, and they note Jack's nicknames Jackson and Gate.
266.ch: New Orleans ballrooms and Tony Almerico
266.q: Anyone who was older than you was Mr. and if you grew up with them, I would have been a little bit more. And if you grew up with them, it was still Mr. if somebody was 15 years older than you. It was hard making the transition from Mr. Allen to Dick or Richard. Because it just became a habit.…

907.t: Name Buddy Burton and recording under Ink Williams
907.s: Burton explains how his nickname became his professional name at his first recording and that he was under Ink Williams's contract for ten years.
907.q: Okay, Buddy Burton's my name. I have recorded so on and so on. Now, cut. I'm very proud to tell you that my name is Buddy Burton, and that's my professional name when I first started recording records. And so I've been using that away from that clean up until now. What is your full name? And my…

268.t: Kid Thomas's real name and musicians' nicknames
268.s: Talk about Joseph Butler as Kid Thomas and nicknames, including Whipple and Egg for Turner.
268.ch: Sonny South breakup and small bands
268.q: This brother has so many nicknames, yeah, Kid Twat. Joseph Butler. Did you have a nickname too? Outside of Benny. Everybody calls him Benny Tony. Everybody got nicknames. You know, I never have understood how people look each other up in the phone book if they

181.t: How the Eureka got its name
181.s: Parker explains he heard the name Eureka from men he worked with in a yard and used it for his band.
181.q: I don't know I'm the one giving it. Yes. I listen. They had some... I used to bum in a yard down there. And they had some watched indie boys you know? Yes. And they all, they were musicians. But they didn't let, I didn't let them know I could play you know? So I used to, they used to make a drink…

398.t: Fresh fish and Reptimers: prison terms for new and old inmates
398.s: Maxey explains that a fresh fish is a newcomer and old hands are called Reptimers, Lifetimers or old Ace; Allen checks the pronunciation.
398.q: What do you call him? Well, a fella's been here for a long time. Some of them call him old Reptimers. Some of them call him Lifetimers. Some of them call him old Ace. Well, you know that he's not a fresh fish.

892.t: Why the book is titled Oh, Didn't He Ramble?
892.s: The title is the song played returning from the cemetery, and also fits Lee's rambling, wild youth.
892.q: And, but, oh, didn't he ramble doesn't mean, but it meant that he was the one that did a lot of rambling around. Yeah. And so that's why he put the title, oh, didn't he ramble? Yeah.

653.s: Opening of reel one; Batiste gives his name and explains the variant spellings Baptiste, Batiste and Battiste.
653.q: The other T is B-A-T-T-I-S-T-E. There's not that many families that spell it like that here. But there is another family that's B-A-P-T-I-S-T-E. That's Baptiste. That is the original way of spelling it. The way my name is spelled is like the material.

22.t: Tunes with no names: 'play some dirt'
22.s: He says the band called tunes 'dirt', then they briefly discuss the vulgar language.
22.ch: Tiger Rag and Mopah Blues explained
22.q: No, see, outside of Hunyadi. They didn't even know how he called Hunyadi. They didn't know. They just said, play some Dirt.

275.t: Origin of the name 'Mr. Bourbon Street'
275.s: He explains his nickname and a walk down Bourbon Street with newspaper reporters.
275.q: Well, yes, because I'm from this part of the country and from the south where all this jazz and blues originated. And every place I go, well, they always refer to me as Mr. Bourbon Street himself. And my Dixieland jazz and blues and coon shouting and my flash and rhythm tap dancing. Which, it's an…

43.s: She explains the billing 'Miles of smiles' and her real name, Elizabeth Landreau and then Pajot. Willie Pajot was her husband's first cousin.
43.ch: Childhood and early career in New Orleans
43.q: Well, they said, just like for a good billing, they'd say, Miles, I used to be smiling all the time. They said, Miles of smiles from Lizzie Miles. But my name is Elizabeth. Elizabeth Mary Landreau. That's my maiden name. And then my marriage name is Elizabeth Pajot.

44.t: How Maxey got the name Hogman
44.s: Maxey tells the story of doctoring hogs as a boy, earning the name Hog Man.
44.q: Well... That was kind of a short name that they gave me. They was, uh... I always believed that I was a hog doctor and I... So I started off doctoring on hogs, and every time Dad would get a bunch of pigs and they'd leave home, I'd give a hog doctor. So I messed around, I think I killed about half…

152.t: How he got the name Red and being called Alvin
152.s: He explains that Red refers to light skin in black culture, how billing as Red Tyler made it stick, and who still calls him Alvin.
152.ch: Dew Drop and the name Red
152.q: Okay, uh, it was probably during the time I, I, uh, started at Grunwald School of Music. And I don't know who started that. But the thing is, most whites don't understand why they call me Red.

629.s: Picou explains his godfather, who was an undertaker, and how Floreston and Piku became Alphonse.
629.q: My Godfather used to be a great undertaker on Ramport and... Well, this street here... Well, they changed the two names. No. Governor Nichols. Governor Nichols. But it wasn't Governor Nichols at that time. Hospital. Hospital. Okay, I guess it's going again. You were talking about your... Your…

432.t: Miss Maggie's and Father Allen's Globetrotters
432.s: He explains his band name and the St. Monica's contest.
432.q: It could have been a joint. I know Miss Isabel, I know she on Chinatown, couldn't be talking about that. Well who had the band called the Globetrotters here? I did Father Allen's Globetrotters.

664.t: How Cats Mistrey got his nickname
664.s: Artigues explains the Jewish-sounding joke on a picnic trip that gave drummer Harold Mistrey the nickname Cats.
664.q: to play on all that picnic one morning dick and it stuck time like blue we're going out the lake and he had a straw hat on and he looked just the part of a jew i said say is you the son oh you the son of israel cats and that name stuck time man till this day everybody knows him about cats like…

800.t: Nicknames Tats and Biscuit; his father's Creole French
800.s: He explains Tats came from his short father, Biscuit from his cracker-factory work, and that his father spoke Creole French.
800.q: Yeah, I play. I play Little Jones. I play Little Jones. I play Little Jones. You play Carnicle Day, you say? The last Jones plays Carnicle Day. Well, I was going to ask, where did you get that name Taz? How did you? I called my dad at that. My dad was named Taton. Because he was short. He was…

590.t: Why Armstrong was the greatest; Bing Crosby and nicknames
590.s: Alcorn calls Louis the greatest because he changed the pattern of singing and playing, and discusses the nickname Pops or Satchmo.
590.q: I say Lewis was the greatest because he was a starlet He had his own way of playing And he was the guy that turned his trim He made the sound of the trumpet They had good trumpet players back in the years

713.t: Uncle's full name: Butler Rap, nicknamed Gaiye
713.s: Nelson says his uncle's name was Butler Rap, nicknamed Gaiye, and no one knows what the nickname means.
713.ch: Second reel: instrument, style and wrap-up
713.q: Gaiye. Sounds like it might mean gay or something, I don't know. Yeah, it probably does. Maybe somebody will know someday.

482.t: Researcher asks Walter Lewis about Stormy Weather and the Tulane and Broad record
482.s: The interviewer explains how he traced Stormy Weather's Jackson, Mississippi records to New Orleans; Walter Lewis knows him only by nickname as a boogie-woogie blues player.
482.q: No, let me see. I don't know what his real name was. That was his nickname. A lot of them guys just knew him about his nickname. You don't know his real name. I don't know what his real name was. But they used to call him Stormy Weather. He used to boogie woogie. He used to love to play the boogie…

121.t: What he was called as a child and how Tommy Ridgley became his name
121.s: Family called him Thomas; the professional name Tommy Ridgley was chosen in Mr. Levy's office with Dave Bartholomew, and he spells out Ridgley.
121.q: When I got in the music business and when I went to record, I went to Mr. Levy's office with Dave Bartholomew. And we sat down and I signed all these papers. You know, if I had a hit record I wouldn't have got no money I guess. Same way. But anyway, they discussed a professional name. And so he…

190.t: Why Purnell is called Wiggles; Ransom the bassist
190.s: Purnell explains he got the nickname Wiggles on a riverboat because he could not keep still, and the name was spread by the bassist Ransom, now in Chicago.
190.q: Oh, well, see when I first got, when I first sent it from him, well, I could never keep still, see, when I'd be playing music. So when I went on the boat up in Peoria, and I started playing, man, I started band now, you know, man. Boy, I was just getting that. So I was sitting there, take a solo,…

182.t: Kid Albert's Jazz Band and his nicknames
182.s: Interviewers show an old card for Kid Albert's Jazz Band; he explains he was called Tom Albert, Kid Albert, and played cornet.
182.q: Yeah, it has a kind of carnet. And I wonder, it says, Kid Albert's Jazz Band. Kid Albert, yeah. Well, yeah. Let's see, where were you living then? That was on, um... Uh, 28th, what's that? 2610? Uptown, 8th Street.

794.s: The interviewer asks about donkey derbies; Stagg explains the rural English tradition and the Paragon Stakes named after Mike Casimir's brass band.
794.ch: Barry Martin and New Orleans tours to England
794.q: The donkey derbies? Well, the donkey derbies sort of originated in rural England, way back now, probably in the late 1880s, where they have a group of donkeys, and usually children are jockeys, and they name all these donkeys, and they name their races. They're like a small horse race, and they run…

282.t: How he got the name Jim Little
282.s: His grandfather George Robinson called Jim Robinson Jim Crow and Brown Jim Little to tell the two apart.
282.q: Oh, well Jim and I got that name together. See, my grandpa, he named Jim Crow. And me, Jim Little. And see, they had two Jims around the house. And he had to make a difference. And he got one crow and one little.

283.t: Name Pecoraro and the nickname Peck
283.s: Pecora explains his surname, how Johnny Vittroy began calling him Peck, and why he kept Santo in New Orleans after Chicago and California.
283.q: So, what is your real name? My last name is Pecoraro, but I cut it down to Pecoraro. You just called yourself Santa Pecoraro? Yes, and it's a funny thing, then it was about 19, oh, let me see, 19, 20, around 20, Johnny Vittroy started calling me Peck instead of Pecoraro, see? And then when I went…

286.s: Russ was featured as a singer under the name Kid Nats and got the nickname Shaker while playing with Captain Handley.
286.q: Yes, I was playing during my, I used to sing. Takes so long for them, gentlemen. They'd feature me as Kid Nats. You know who they're talking about? Kid which? Kid Nats. No.

649.t: Alan Shaw and Peetie Wheatstraw as one man
649.s: Interviewer and Slim discuss whether Alan Shaw and Peetie Wheatstraw were the same man and where he came from.
649.q: Now that I don't know. But I see them in Memphis, I see them in St. Louis. I don't guess you're going to pay that. Because he used to live in East St. Louis. That's a woman, brother, you know. You know how he's going to live. So I don't know. It sure don't want to. It sure don't want to. It won't…

591.t: Passport trouble and the spelling of his name
591.s: Difficulty with his birth certificate and passport; his French name Goudie and Francis/Frank.

91.q: sure, but I do know that at one period, Irving Mills was talking about the idea of having -- what was it -- the Royal Orchestra, Inc. --and he was ... I think the idea stemmed from having Duke Ellington.

233.t: How Monk got his nickname; his brothers' real names
233.s: Monk does not know who named him; Wes was really John Leslie and Buddy is Charles.
233.q: Yeah, I was named Monk but I don't know who named me. I tried to trace it back, but Monk is all I was ever accustomed to hearing.

18.t: J. C. Higginbotham Jr. and the nickname Cricket
18.s: His son explains he got the name Cricket from being an active baby.
18.ch: Favorite bands, advice and family reflections
18.q: Just being an active baby, you know. They couldn't think of anything else that was that active.

29.t: Why they called him Mr. Paul
29.s: Collette asks about another trumpeter named Paul; Howard says he is the only Paul and everyone called him Mr. Paul.
29.ch: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
29.q: Yeah, Mr. -- that's what they did, they always used to call me Mr. Paul. I don't know why they did that.

95.t: Texas Nightingale and Illinois Songbird nicknames
95.s: She explains how newspapers and Okeh gave her the names Texas Nightingale and Illinois Songbird.
95.q: Some other paper (unintelligible). They say, I didn't come from Chicago, I came from Texas. (Unintelligible). And Texas say I come from Texas (unintelligible).

168.t: How Slim and Slam got their name, with Martin Block

389.t: Glen Gray's nickname Spike and the Venuti connection
389.s: Glen Gray was called Spike, and Venuti had played in the Goldkette band before Challis.
389.q: Oh, yeah. And I remember a time when I had rejoined the Casa Loma, that it, it was then called the Glen Gray Orchestra, down in Miami.

76.t: Jazz slang: bring down, drag, swing them into bad health
76.s: Marge and Dance trade slang such as bring down, drag and swinging them into bad health, and Paul Gonsalves objecting to calling someone a drag.
76.ch: Chicago memories and the road to the Navy
76.q: A lot of people can't remember the 'bring down.' You know, like you know you was having to explain it to old Bert the other day what 'bring down' means. Instead of a drag, you used to say 'bring down'.

238.t: Joe Wynn's nickname and her second husband
238.s: Joe Wynn was nicknamed Windy; her second husband was Leonel Lewis, called Buddy.
238.q: His name was Leonel. They all called him Buddy. Buddy was his nickname.

7.s: Thomas says small shoes caused foot trouble, and Cab's 'Play it, Foots!' stuck; he bought a tenor.

455.s: Budd gives his full name and explains his uncle nicknamed him Butterbeans, later shortened to Budd.
455.q: called me Butterbeans, so later on in the years, as I grew up, as a little fellow, and they cut it short for Budd. And that's how I got that nickname. So now I always say Albert B-u-d-d, Budd, Johnson, and Budd is my professional name.

171.t: Spook breakfasts and McShann's nickname Hootie
171.s: Spook breakfasts were all-night jam sessions; 'spook' meant ghost, and Jay McShann was Hootie for staying up like an owl.
171.q: And sometimes it was, you know, but not understood as that in Kansas City. In what's his name -- the term that was used in Kansas City was more or less the ghost, you know, the spook. Anybody who stayed up that late was a ghost.
